hypothesis: Linux release install footprint is dominated by line-table DWARF in the linked ELF; separate decoder and strip debug sections of the SAME linked image to reduce delivered bytes while keeping function names and offline file:line recovery.
approach: Option C: release build keeps line tables and does not strip at link; scripts/release/split_debug.py derives gzip decoder and separate shipped ELF from one immutable linked Cargo image, with objcopy --only-keep-debug then objcopy --strip-debug --remove-section=.debug_gdb_scripts. Linux release and continuous workflows run split before assembly; release promotes gzip decoder as separate per-tag asset (not rolling nightly). assemble_artifacts.py hard-fails decoder-like sidecars inside staged/packed payload; channel manifest rejects decoder references. Assembler binds decoder SHA/build-ID to shipped ELF, promotion verifies exact decoder SHA and installed tar ELF SHA/build-ID, SHA256SUMS and provenance cover the per-tag decoder; rolling nightly checksum lists tarballs only. Option A (strip all) rejected: loses backtrace symbol names. Option B (strip=debuginfo at link) rejected: it preserves function names but omits a same-build decoder, so shipped file:line cannot be restored from an independently linked binary (the .text differed in tested link configurations).
parity_notes: RLM API/wire/session replay source untouched; all lane changes limited to Cargo.toml release profile, scripts/release, and Linux release/CI workflows. Linux ELF static .symtab/function names and .dynsym are kept; shipped backtraces lose file:line but detached same-image decoder restores them via addr2line. GLIBC release gate still inspects .dynsym. macOS unchanged (line tables kept); dSYM extraction is follow-up, macOS bytes not measured. Linux x64 measurement only; Linux arm64 workflow wired but not measured.
